comment: The Benefits Package Registry appropriately separates authoritative benefit definitions from operational claims and payment functions. It may be useful to make explicit that confirmation of coverage, eligibility, provider status and technical validity of a transaction does not necessarily establish that sufficient evidence exists to support a consequential claim or payment decision.

public.text: The Benefits Package Registry appropriately separates authoritative benefit definitions from operational claims and payment functions. It may be useful to make explicit that confirmation of coverage, eligibility, provider status and technical validity of a transaction does not necessarily establish that sufficient evidence exists to support a consequential claim or payment decision.
public.suggestedRevision: Consider clarifying that, where claims or other financing decisions depend on evidence of service delivery or fulfilment of programme conditions, countries should define where responsibility for assessing the sufficiency and provenance of that evidence resides within the financing architecture. Confirmation of coverage, eligibility or technical validity should not, by itself, be interpreted as establishing that all substantive requirements for payment or other consequential action have been satisfied.
